newsitem.title: SENEGAL: Gambia candidate takes refuge at Senegal embassy.
newsitem.headline: Gambia candidate takes refuge at Senegal embassy.

text.p: Lawyer Ousainou Darboe, main rival to Gambia's military leader Yahya Jammeh in the presidential election, has taken refuge in Senegal's embassy in the Gambian capital Banjul, official Senegalese sources said on Friday.

Darboe had been in the embassy with members of his family since Thursday evening when polls closed and vote counting began in the election designed to restore the tiny West African country to civilian rule, the sources said.
Jammeh, who toppled civilian independence president Sir Dawda Jawara in 1994, led the four-man field with results from over half the constituencies officially declared.
Electoral officials said Jammeh, 31, had 76,790 votes to Darboe's 58,356 but commentators said the race was still open as results had not been announced for two of Darboe's strongholds.
The Senegalese sources said that Darboe, 48-year-old vice-president of the Gambia Bar Association, was at the embassy with his two wives and three children.
Gambia, born of 19th century Anglo-French colonial rivalry, won independence from Britain in 1965 and is surrounded by Francophone Senegal apart from a stretch of Atlantic coastline.

Jawara survived a coup attempt by leftists in 1981 thanks to the intervention of Senegalese troops. The abortive coup, in which hundreds of people died, prompted Jawara to sign a loose confederation treaty with Senegal.
The pact collapsed in 1989 with Gambia reluctant to speed up trade and customs union for fear of losing its identity.
